rendered: The document does not say the authors chose a long melt-diffusion step. It mentions that duration only as a feature of other, conventional methods. The paper states that those other methods traditionally employ long (>20 h) melt[1] techniques to ensure pore infiltration[2]. The authors instead used an isothermal vapor phase process[3] run at low temperature (175 °C)[4] and lasting 1 h[5]. Their stated reason is that this method is significantly more scalable and less expensive compared to[6] the long melt methods. The only temperature the document gives for a melt-type route is the alternative of temperature (>300 °C) loadings[7], which is used for depolymerization of sulfur. No temperature is given for the long melt-diffusion step itself.
